title: 2001 HMMT February Algebra Problem 10
statement: Find the real solutions of \((2 x+1)(3 x+1)(5 x+1)(30 x+1)=10\).

solutions.text: \((2 x+1)(3 x+1)(5 x+1)(30 x+1)=[(2 x+1)(30 x+1)][(3 x+1)(5 x+1)]=\) \(\left(60 x^{2}+32 x+1\right)\left(15 x^{2}+8 x+1\right)=(4 y+1)(y+1)=10\), where \(y=15 x^{2}+8 x\). The quadratic equation in \(y\) yields \(y=1\) and \(y=-\frac{9}{4}\). For \(y=1\), we have \(15 x^{2}+8 x-1=0\), so \(x=\frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{31}}{15}\). For \(y=-\frac{9}{4}\), we have \(15 x^{2}+8 x+\frac{9}{4}\), which yields only complex solutions for \(x\). Thus the real solutions are \(\frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{31}}{15}\).
